articleTitle: An efficient algorithm to remove electrocardiogram from diaphragmatic electromyography by using wavelet spectrum and secant method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: An efficient algorithm based on wavelet spectrum and secant method is proposed, investigated and exploited for removing electrocardiogram(ECG) from diaphragmatic electromyography(EMGdi). As a strong interference, ECG has the high amplitude and spectrum overlap in raw EMGdi. Inspired from the characteristic of ECG, low frequency wavelet spectrum of raw EMGdi and gate function are used for fixing the peak position of QRS wave. After calculating the undisturbed average energy at the neighborhood of the R peak in the field of wavelet spectrum, the threshold adaptive criterion employs undisturbed energy to match the energy of ECG interference interval and shrink those interference coefficients. The optimal thresholds in each ECG interference are derived from secant method. In comparing with other de-noising algorithms, the processed results of simulated EMGdi signal and clinical respiratory signals show that the wavelet spectrum and secant method proposed in this paper can remove ECG interference in respiratory signals effectively and reserve its signal characteristics satisfyingly.

articleTitle: The Impact of Regenerative Braking in Electric Vehicles to Energy-efficient Routing Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Regenerative braking has been demonstrated as an effective way in prolonging the mileages of electric vehicle (EV). In this paper, we aim to examine a generic research problem on how to better utilise the regenerative braking for energy efficiency when routing EV. To this end, we consider a Markov decision process (MDP) based model with 4 distinct reward functions to plan the paths for the EV to traverse a hilly landscape. The results show that by using net energy used as the reward function, the most energy-efficient path can be found. In addition, taking proactive detours can be an energy-efficient way to either avoid excessive energy consumption or prompt energy regeneration.

articleTitle: Predicting the Energy Meter Demand by a Window-based Gradient Boosting Regression Tree Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: The accurate prediction of energy meter demand is crucial for the formulation of the energy meter purchasing management plan of the metering centers, leading to effective reduction in distribution and storage costs. In this study, we use a window-based Gradient Boosting Regression Tree(GBRT(W-b)) prediction model for the forecast of energy meter demand. The model is used to train and fit historical data about the numbers of monthly newly installed energy meters in Fujian Province, China. We compare the prediction results obtained using the GBRT(W-b) model with those from Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average(ARIMA). The experimental results demonstrate that GBRT(W-b) outperforms the ARIMA model in forecasting the total amount of newly installed energy meters for the next three months, next six months, and next nine months. This also indicates that the proposed prediction method based on GBRT(W-b) achieves high prediction accuracy and can assist power grid companies in improving their purchasing management of energy meters.

articleTitle: Electrical Equipment Fault Diagnosis: A Technique Combining Fuzzy Logic and Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Diagnosing faults in electrical equipment is a complex task that requires precise and adaptive decision-making. Traditional methodologies often fall short in handling the inherent uncertainties and vagueness associated with such diagnosis. In this paper, we introduce a novel technical approach that synergistically combines fuzzy logic with large language models, specifically ChatGLM2-6B. Fuzzy logic provides a structured framework to deal with imprecise information, while the language model offers a deep understanding of textual data related to faults. By taking local electrical text descriptions as input, we harness the power of fuzzy inference systems and the language model to generate comprehensive and accurate fault diagnosis results. This innovative fusion promises a more robust and adaptive fault diagnosis mechanism, ensuring safer and more efficient electrical infrastructure operations.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a lightweight advertising system based on Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: The combination of remote advertisement placement and smart city brings new opportunities and challenges for outdoor advertisement placement in cities. This paper proposes a lightweight advertising system based on Internet of Things and edge computing, which includes three layers: a cloud platform, an edge control terminal and IoT devices including dimming glass and smart projectors. The cloud platform manages the advertisement resources, sends out the play schedule and completes the identity authentication of the edge control terminal. The edge control terminal controls the addressing and networking of the play media consisting of dimming glass and smart projector, and carries out identity registration. At the same time, it completes the switching of the transmittance of the dimming glass and the signal synchronisation of the advertisements, then broadcasts the advertisements according to the schedule. The lightweight communication protocol MQTT is used between the layers to reduce the overhead of data transmission. Experiments show that the lightweight advertising system can manage and play advertisements efficiently with low latency and provide users with a good viewing experience.

articleTitle: Consumer and Industrial Mobile Robot Navigation Based on Evidential Multi-Granularity Three-Way Decisions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: In the context of consumer and industrial applications, mobile robot navigation (MRN) has become a revolutionary advancement. This technology enables robots to execute a wide range of tasks in complex factory environments, ensuring highly precise path planning and navigation. More importantly, MRN systems help reduce the risk of human errors and workplace accidents, thus creating a safer and more dependable working environment. However, during the testing process of MRN, the data involved often exhibit imprecise and uncertain characteristics. To address this challenge, the introduction of q-rung orthopair fuzzy sets (q-ROFSs) has been employed, integrating q-ROFSs with MRN. This unique fusion enhances the system’s flexibility, providing a clear advantage in the consumer and industrial sector. Hence, it becomes particularly essential to put forth a novel three-way group decision rule within the q-ROF information system, aiming to further enhance the efficiency and reliability of MRN systems in consumer and industrial applications. This research is expected to offer innovative solutions for the future development of the consumer and industrial sector. Initially, the integration of the q-rung orthopair fuzzy (q-ROF) concept with multi-granularity three-way decisions resulted in the formulation of adjustable multi-granularity q-ROF probabilistic rough sets. Following this, an optimal granularity selection was conducted using evidence reasoning methods. Finally, the developed approach was applied to a case study in MRN.

articleTitle: Height estimation and the number of trees in transmission line corridors based on multi-source data fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: The safe operation of transmission lines depends largely on the cleaning and protection of the corridors. The tall trees in the corridors have a great impact on the safety of transmission lines. The statistics of tree information of transmission line corridor is of great significance to the compensation work of transmission line and the confirmation of disputes between the participating parties. In this paper, a method of tree number height estimation based on multi-source data fusion is proposed, which makes comprehensive use of the advantages of image data and laser point cloud data to improve the accuracy of tree number and height information in complex scenarios of transmission line corridors. The accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified by comparing the automatic calculation results with the manual statistics results. The results show that the proposed method has the characteristics of small error and high efficiency, and is conducive to the statistics of tree information in the acceptance of transmission line corridors.

articleTitle: A CNN-LSTM-Based Model for Predicting Monthly Power Capacity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: With the growing demand for electricity and the increasing importance of environmental sustainability, energy efficiency has become a key factor for the sustainable development of power systems. As an effective tool, power forecasting can help power companies and government departments to better plan and manage energy resources and achieve efficient use of energy. In this paper, an improved forecasting model, the hybrid CNN-LSTM model combined with clustering algorithm based on K-means, is proposed to forecast monthly power demand. In the case of insufficient training data, clustering algorithm is used to augment the existing data to improve the prediction accuracy of the hybrid CNN-LSTM model. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can indeed improve the prediction accuracy based on the data from agriculture and industry sectors in a province of East China.

articleTitle: Research on Reducing the Resonance Frequency of Low Frequency Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Metamaterials, as a new type of material for manufacturing electromagnetic and electronic devices, have become the focus of many studies. It can be used in many disciplines, such as chemistry, physics, materials science, optoelectronics, semiconductor science, and equipment manufacturing, and are currently a cutting-edge and strategically significant research topic. Electromagnetic metamaterials are a new type of artificial composite electromagnetic material with controllable dielectric constant and magnetic permeability. This paper establishes a theoretical framework for metamaterials, divides electromagnetic wave media into four quadrants using constitutive parameters, and introduces the calculation method of effective magnetic permeability. This paper is based on a square planar spiral structure. In order to reduce the resonant frequency, a quantitative analysis was conducted on the influence of double-layer mirror structure, patch resistance, and different stacking structures on the resonant frequency. The reference resonant frequency was reduced from 9.6MHz to 7.6MHz, providing a solid foundation for subsequent research.

articleTitle: An Extended Inverse Reinforcement Learning Control For Target-Expert Systems With Different Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: This paper proposes an extended inverse Reinforcement Learning (EIRL) control to drive a target system following an expert system with different parameters in their dynamic. By learning the state weights in the linear quadratic cost function to find optimal control gains from knowledge of a given expert trajectory, a quasi-optimal control for a target system can be iteratively calculated without a necessary condition that the target-expert systems have identical dynamic, which is required in the published papers. Accordingly, we extend the algorithm to calculate an inverse optimal weight of the linear quadratic cost function to find an optimal control for the target system. Furthermore, we proof the convergence of EIRL. Lastly an illustrative simulation is tested to verify the effectiveness and virtues of the proposed method, specifically which is more adaptive for obtaining optimal trajectories of the target system from an expert system without identical dynamic.

articleTitle: ComESN: Compressive Echo State Network for Multi-task Time-series Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Time-series prediction has been widely studied for single-variable applications, but shows poor performance for multi-variable applications due to the complex correlation. Multivariable prediction is often transferred into many single-variable tasks, and results into high computational cost. The prediction performance decreases exponentially as the dimensions increase. The compression of multiple prediction tasks is necessary to provide a trade-off between computational cost and prediction accuracy. For this purpose, compressive echo state neural network (ComESN) is proposed, which consists of a compressive module and a multi-task echo state network (MT-ESN). In this study, the locally linear embedding algorithm is adopted as compression method to reduce the number of prediction tasks for improving the computational efficiency. A novel MT-ESN is developed to further improve the performance of ESN for multi-task prediction. Due to highly efficient compression and unveiling correlation of multiple tasks, ComESN could cut down the computational cost while providing a promising prediction accuracy. Experiments on three real-world datasets illustrate that the proposed ComESN could compete with state-of-the-art methods with regard to computational cost and accuracy.

articleTitle: Periodic Analysis of Meter Installation data in Fujian Province based on Spectral Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Electricity meters are critical measuring devices in power systems used for recording electricity consumption and monitoring power usage. However, the installation patterns and periodicities of electricity meters remain inadequately explored. This paper employs spectral analysis to analyze historical electricity meter installation data from Fujian province, revealing distinct periodic patterns across different regions, meter types, and installation processes. The results demonstrate evident periodic characteristics in various regions of Fujian province, with different meter types exhibiting diverse periodic patterns. Moreover, variations in installation processes also impact the observed periodicities. These findings hold significant implications for optimizing electricity meter installation processes and ensuring the sustainable development of power systems.

articleTitle: An Approximation Technique for Solving Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control Problems Using Chebyshev Polynomials*
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: We introduce an innovative numerical method for addressing Linear-Quadratic optimal control problems that come with control constraints. Initially, we reframe the LQ optimal control problem into an unconstrained problem by utilizing the constraint transcription technique. Next, we employ Chebyshev series to approximate both the state and control functions. To bolster the approximation precision, Chebyshev series are further leveraged to approximate the coefficient functions inherent to the linear dynamic system. According to the unique attributes of Chebyshev polynomials, the approximate problem can be seamlessly converted into a corresponding quadratic programming problem. As a result, any feasible solution to the approximate problem guarantees compliance with its dynamic system throughout the complete time horizon. To substantiate the effectiveness of our proposed methodology, we’ve tested it on a real-world scenario. The computational results underscore that our method outperforms the Chebyshev pseudo-spectral method in terms of approximation accuracy.

articleTitle: Analysis of the cyclical change in the capacity of business expansion based on spectral analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: The business expansion of business-oriented electrical facilities plays a crucial role in shaping the future retail electricity market. Understanding the cyclical patterns of business expansion capacity is essential for enhancing the efficiency of the power system, improving power planning, and fostering industry development. To shed light on this subject, this study analyzes the monthly business expansion capacity data from January 2016 to November 2022 in a certain province of eastern China. Using spectral analysis methods, the findings reveal that, significant annual cyclical patterns exist in business expansion types of all industries except for the financial sector. Moreover, specific industries and business expansion types also exhibit quarterly, four-month, and biannual cycles in their monthly business expansion capacity data. On the other hand, we attempt to apply clustering methods to the data, obtaining industry results that exhibit similar cyclic patterns. Overall, this study offers valuable insights into the cyclical nature of business expansion capacity. The identified patterns can serve as a foundation for improving power system efficiency, facilitating effective power planning, and enabling the development of the industry.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Visual Operation and Maintenance Technology for Conveyor Belt in Catalyst Workshop
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Reducing energy consumption, increasing production yield, and maintaining the continuous, stable, and efficient operation of catalyst production line systems are primary requirements and current challenges for catalyst factories. However, catalyst production often faces issues such as conveyor belt misalignment and breakage, which can lead to decreased production efficiency and lower product quality. To tackle these challenges, this paper proposes a machine vision-based monitoring and control system. Specifically, a binocular camera is employed to detect AprilTag labels and measure the offset of the conveyor belt, while also providing real-time depth information of the conveyor belt skirt edge. Compared to traditional machine vision approaches, this system demonstrates higher accuracy, stability, and improved production efficiency and product quality.

articleTitle: Intelligent Retrieval and Question Answering Technology for Power Grid Security Standards: A Brief Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: With the rapid development of information technology, the smart and digital transformation of power grid has become an inevitable trend. However, this trend has brought about increasingly large and complex power grid security standard documents, posing significant challenges to power grid research and management. In order to effectively address the risks and issues related to power grid security management, this paper aims to conduct in-depth research on the intelligent retrieval and question answering techniques for power grid security standards, exploring how to intelligently process and apply power grid security standard documents.

articleTitle: A Joint Design of Path Planning and Lane Reservation for Emergency Service in ITS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Reaching the accident scene promptly for emergency vehicles (EVs) can significantly alleviate the negative impact of accidents. However, finding a way to reduce the response time of EVs (i.e., the travel time of an EV to reach the rescue location) remains a challenge that needs to be addressed. In this paper, we design a distributed intelligent transportation system (DITS) powered by vehicular fog computing (VFC), which offers new possibilities for designing traffic scheduling methods. We propose a soft actor-critic-based EV rapid passage approach (SACRP) to minimize the response time of EVs. The collaborative lane reservation module uses the latest traffic data to create a traffic dispatch strategy to reserve empty lane. Subsequently, we propose a soft actor-critic-based algorithm as the real-time path planning module. The path planning module integrates vital road information, such as lane reservation priority, real-time road data, EV location, and traffic signal information. The path planning module strategically plans the path with the shortest response time for the EV. We conduct extensive experiments to evaluate the performance of the proposed method, and the results show that the response time for EVs could be reduced by 24.6% compared to the latest study.

articleTitle: Event-Based Pinning Synchronization in Delayed Dynamical Networks With Stochastic Noises
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: This work investigates the synchronization problem in a class of dynamical network with stochastic noises in the couplings, where each node has delayed dynamics, and some pinning controllers are assigned to a portion of nodes. In order to reduce the redundant update of the control, an event-triggering mechanism is applied to synchronize the entire network. Based on the stability theory of delayed stochastic differential equation, some sufficient condition is derived to guarantee successful synchronization in mean square sense under the proposed control scheme. Some numerical simulations are given to demonstrate the validity of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Rotated quaternion valued algebra and its application to discrete time rotated quaternion valued Fourier transform based human signal processing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: This paper proposes the concept of the rotated quaternion valued algebra and its application to the human signal processing. The conventional quaternion valued number consists of three pure imaginary components. They are the i component, the j component and the k component. These three components can be understood as these three standard principal axes in the Cartesian coordinate, in which they are orthogonal one another. In this paper, these three principal axes are rotated via multiplying to three rotational matrices. Here, these three rotational matrices perform the rotations with respect to these three principal axes, respectively. Now, the conventional discrete time quaternion valued Fourier transform is extended to the discrete time rotated quaternion valued Fourier transform based on the rotated quaternion valued system. For performing the denoising of the human signals, since the transform involves three rotational angles, the design of these three rotational angles is formulated as a nonconvex optimization problem. In particular, the objective is to minimize the total number of the transformed coefficients. In fact, this optimization problem is nonsmooth and nonconvex. To address these difficulties, an L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> searching points algorithm is employed for finding the nearly global optimal solution of the optimization problem. To perform the regression, the features are extracted based on the various values of the rotational angles. Then, the random forest is employed for performing the feature selection. This technique is applied to perform the non-invasive blood glucose estimation. The computer numerical simulation results show that the estimation accuracy is significantly improved.

Author Keywords: discrete time rotated quaternion valued Fourier transform

articleTitle: Advancing Fire Safety in Hong Kong Buildings: An IoT-Based Fire Accident Indication System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: This study focuses on the development of an innovative fire accident indication system for buildings in Hong Kong, leveraging the Internet of Things (IoT) technology. The proposed system integrates IoT devices and sensors to enable real-time monitoring, early fire detection, and prompt notification of fire incidents. By utilizing the power of interconnected devices and data analytics, the system enhances fire safety measures, improves emergency response time, and minimizes potential damage. The research considers the unique characteristics and challenges of Hong Kong's urban environment, including high population density and complex building structures. The outcomes of this study contribute to advancing fire safety standards and emergency management practices in Hong Kong, with potential applications in other regions facing similar circumstances.

articleTitle: Integrating Functional Safety into Hazard-Based Safety Engineering: Towards a Comprehensive Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: As the convergence between hardware and software and the corresponding complexity escalates, the adequacy of safety standards should be reevaluated. The first Hazard-based Safety Engineering (HBSE) standard, IEC 62368-1, despite its comprehensive focus on protection against hazards such as fire, overcurrent, and overtemperature, lacks explicit inclusion of Functional Safety requirements when those safety protections are software-controlled. This paper is a pioneering attempt to present the rationale, assessment process, and nomological validity for incorporating Functional Safety principles into IEC 62368-1 by proposing a potential comprehensive framework that combines HBSE and RBSE, and this will maximize the potential of cutting-edge technologies implemented in ICT products, including the latest generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), and dynamic safety design such as telemetry-based failure prediction.

articleTitle: Enhancing Navigation Aids Status Recognition Based on Extended Space Forest and Time Domain Features Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Navigation aids can help ships find the correct waterway and indicate dangerous areas in the channel, ensuring safe passage for vessels. To address the problem of sparse feature numbers in collected navigation aids data, this paper proposes a model called TDES-RF, which is based on extended space forest and the fusion of time domain features. Four feature generating operators in the extended space forest are used to expand the original feature set, generating different expansion spaces for each base classifier. In addition, time domain features fusion captures dynamic changes and time correlation of data, enriching feature information for more accurate classification. The results show that the accuracy of navigation aids state recognition using random forest as the base model is only 79.88%. After adopting extended space forest and time domain features fusion separately, the accuracy of state recognition improves by 0.12% and 3.33% compared to the base model respectively. Finally, combining these two methods, our model achieves the highest accuracy among all state recognition models at 84.17%.

articleTitle: Generative AI Enables EEG Data Augmentation for Alzheimer’s Disease Detection Via Diffusion Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a non-invasive method to measure the electrical activity of the brain and can be regarded as an effective means of diagnosing Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, The diagnosis of AD based on EEG often encounters the problem of data scarcity. For deep learning models, data scarcity problems lead to overfitting of the model, making it impossible to build effective, highly accurate, and stable models. Data augmentation is often used as an effective means to solve the problem of data scarcity. In this paper, we propose a diffusion models-based EEG data augmentation framework (Diff-EEG). The proposed framework Vector Quantized Variational autoencoders(VQ-VAE) and guided diffusion models to learn the distribution of limited EEG dataset, thereby generating high-quality artificially synthesized EEG data to supplement the dataset. Finally, the result of experiments demonstrate that our proposed method can generate high-quality artificial EEG data, which can effectively improve the performance of AD diagnosis models.

articleTitle: Design and application of data-driven LESN-DHP controller
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Wastewater treatment processes (WWTP) involve a large number of physical, chemical and biological reactions. The concentration of Dissolved oxygen (DO) is an important water quality parameter in WWTP, so it is necessary to control it. To solve this difficult problem, a dual heuristic programming (DHP) controller based on leakage Echo State Network (LESN) is proposed, which is called LESN-DHP controller for short. Firstly, a neural network (NN) identifier based on LESN (LESN-Identifier) is designed to obtain the dynamic characteristics of the system. Then the stability analysis and convergence analysis are carried out. Finally, the feasibility of LESN-DHP controller is verified by simulation experiment. The simulation experiment proves that LESN-DHP controller has better control effect and better performance index than other controllers in WWTP.

articleTitle: Improved Neural Collaborative Filtering Recommendation Method based on Multi-Head Attention and Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Recommender systems play an important role in personalized recommendations, and neural collaborative filtering models have achieved some success as an effective recommendation method. However, neural collaborative filtering has limitations in feature representation capabilities and interaction relationship modeling, which limit their recommendation accuracy and personalization capability. In order to address this problem, this paper proposes an improved neural collaborative filtering method, called MHAN-MF. In this method, we propose two improvements: (1) by concatenating the user embedding vector, item embedding vector, and the element-wise product of the user and item embedding vector, the concatenated vector is used as the input feature of the Multi-Layer Perceptron(MLP), thereby enriching the input features of the model and improving its expression ability; (2) the introduction of multi-head attention enables the model to focus on different parts of the input features from different perspectives, to better capture relevant features in the data, and to improve the ability to model complex interactions. We experimentally validated the MHANMF method on publicly accessible datasets. The experimental results show that the MHAN-MF method significantly outperforms other methods in terms of recommendation effectiveness, which verifies the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: A Critical Review on Hazard Analysis and Risk Assessment for Development of Wearable Medical Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Many patients suffer from variable chronic illness. In the past, the patients are required to carry out health check in half year or yearly interval. However, the result is only to reflect the instantaneous health index, for example the glucose level in blood. The wearable medical device is a good solution to the medical doctors to understand the patient’s continuous health status. This paper aims to review the different hazard analysis and risk assessment approaches for developing the wearable medical devices. In the beginning, the need for wearable medical devices is discussed, Secondly, the typical product development cycle is reviewed, Thirdly, different hazard analysis and risk assessment approaches are reviewed and summarized. Finally, a conclusion is made to recommend to the developers.

articleTitle: Sequence Residual Frequency Domain Segmentation Temporal Convolutional Network for COVID-19 Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: COVID-19 belongs to a vast group of viruses rapidly disseminating worldwide. The substantial surge in infected individuals has resulted in a strain on medical facilities across the globe. Consequently, precise predictions of case numbers and fatalities can assist governments and various organizations in preplanning response strategies, alleviating the burden on the healthcare system. Deep learning introduces a fresh approach to addressing emerging coronavirus outbreaks. In this study, we present an innovative hybrid framework that combines singular spectrum analysis (SSA), empirical fourier decomposition (EFD), and temporal convolutional network (TCN) for the prediction of COVID-19. To leverage COVID-19 time series data to its fullest extent, we have devised a residual frequency domain segmentation technique by merging SSA and EFD. Through this approach, the initial time series, characterized by intricate fluctuations, can be restructured into subsequences featuring more conspicuous patterns of change. TCN-based models utilize dilated causal convolution and residual connections to encompass both immediate and prolonged dependencies within time series data. To showcase the predictive capabilities of our proposed model, we conduct short, medium, and long-term forecasts for weekly new confirmed cases and deaths, respectively. Experimental reveal that our model outperforms the other seven baseline models in terms of root mean squared logarithmic error (RMSLE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), and pearson correlation coefficient (PCC).

articleTitle: Feature-Ranked Attention-Driven LSTM: A Novel Hybrid Model for Short-Term Stock Price Predictions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Accurate financial market price forecasting helps investors make financial decisions and governments formulate macro-financial policies. To accurately predict the price trend of stocks, a hybrid model combining Random Forest (RF) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network based on Attention Mechanism (AM), called RF-AM-LSTM, is proposed. Firstly, the input features, such as raw historical data, technical indicators and broad market indices, are ranked in importance and the optimal feature subset is filtered by RF. Then, the filtered feature sequences are processed by an AM to increase attention to important features and decrease attention to redundant features. Finally, the processed sequences are input to the LSTM network for the closing price prediction task. Three stocks listed in the Chinese A-share market are selected for stock price forecasting to evaluate the performance of the hybrid model. The experimental results show that the RF-AM-LSTM can effectively achieve short-term stock price forecasts and achieve the best prediction results on all four regression evaluation indicators.

articleTitle: SETRN: A Transform Structure with Adaptive 3D Attention Mechanism and Global Semantic Supervision for Mobile-Captured Retail Receipts Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Retail receipts serve as important vouchers issued by shopping malls. They accurately record key transaction information, enabling effective analysis of user behavior patterns and merchant sales. Data mining and analysis of receipts offer an effective approach to optimize shopping mall operation strategies and enhance consumers’ shopping experience. While the current mainstream text recognition methods for scanned documents perform well, they face significant challenges when applied to receipt images captured by mobile devices, such as cell phones. To achieve greater accuracy, this research proposes a novel method for global semantic feature-based supervised text recognition. It incorporates a 3D attention module to extract high-dimensional visual features and a pure text image supervised encoder to extract global semantic features. The experiment results on both public benchmarks and a large real-world receipt text recognition dataset show that this method is robust and achieves high accuracy.

articleTitle: UAV Trajectory Planning for Data Collection in Internet of Vehicles: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) assisted data transmission is widely adopted in various internet of vehicles (IoV) applications. This paper is dedicated to the study of UAV-assisted data uploading in IoV with trajectory planning by considering factors including the energy consumption of the UAV, probability of reaching the destination, and the amount of collected data. In particular, we first present a system architecture for UAV-assisted vehicular data uploading. Next, we formulate the UAV trajectory planning problem with the goal of maximizing the amount of collected data. On this basis, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based algorithm, named as MACD-TD (maximizing the amount of collected data through trajectory design). Further, we transform the problem into maximizing the accumulative reward. In order to verify the effectiveness of the proposed architecture and algorithm, we built a 3D simulation platform for conducting experimental simulations. Finally, we give an extensive performance assessment and confirmed the efficacy of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Intelligent Sharding Decision for Blockchain-Enabled Industrial IoT Based on A3C Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: As an essential concept and technology, the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is a feasible way for the advancement of industrial digitization, networking and intelligence. However, it brings serious security and privacy risks to industrial data. Blockchain technology can address security and privacy risks into the IIoT effectively, but there are a few nonnegligible questions in the current researches: 1) The scalability of the conventional blockchain system is extremely limited, making it unable to handle the rapid uploading of massive data in the IIoT. 2) The large-scale nature of IIoT and complex consensus procedure of blockchain result in excessive computational overhead. 3) The balance between security and computational efficiency is often ignored. To address these problems, we propose the concept of sharding decision blockchain innovatively and formulate the optimization problem as a Markov decision process (MDP). Besides, the combining of mobile edge computing (MEC) and cloud computing is empowered the computational efficiency in the proposed scheme. An asynchronous advantage actor-critic (A3C) approach is taken into account and used to solve the optimization problem. Experimental results indicate that our proposed scheme provides a significant improvement on the IIoT versus other solutions.

articleTitle: A Privacy-aware Framework for Assessing and Recommending Short Video Advertisement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: With the increasing number of short video platforms, short video advertisements have gained significant importance as a means of dissemination. Given the usual protection of user data, the efficient recommendation of high-quality short video advertisements to the public without relying on additional information becomes an increasingly important issue. To solve this challenge, we put forward a framework for assessing the quality of short videos, utilizing only visual and audio features extracted from the videos as input. In our framework, we employ pre-trained models to extract the features above. To make better use of these two modalities, we also incorporate an attention module and a modality fusion to further improve the performance of our framework. In the end, we use a large number of short video advertisements to evaluate our proposed framework. The experimental results demonstrate that the accuracy of this method can reach 70.45%, which exhibits a considerable improvement compared to the baseline (50.00%).

articleTitle: Synthesis of Biocomposite through Electrospinning and Screw Extruder in Smart Laboratory Safety
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Petroleum-based composites are multifunctional materials for automotive, construction and energy production. The utilization of petroleum-based substances increases the emission of greenhouse gas, CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and results in global warming. Biocomposites are developed for substituting nonrenewable energy resources. Electrospinning and twin-screw extrusion are two of the common manufacturing processes for synthesizing biocomposites. Both manual and automated operations are involved in the production. Potential risks have significant impact on the safety of workers and the workplace. Personal protective equipment, regular maintenance and risk assessments are proposed to minimize the potential hazards. The existing safety measures cooperate with smart safety management help to reduce laboratory accidents. In the near future, robotics can work alongside with the workers to minimize high risks operations in laboratories.

articleTitle: Two-Space Prediction Approach Based Evolutionary Dynamic Multiobjective Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: To tackle dynamic multiobjective optimization problems (DMOPs), researchers have developed many prediction approaches based on dynamic multiobjective evolutionary algorithms (DMOEAs). Howecer, most methods only predict in a single decision or objective space. Most existing prediction methods are generally utilized the historical Pareto optimal solutions (POS) obtained in the decision space to predict the initial population. However, changes in DMOP may happen simultaneously in both decision and objective spaces. Therefore, predicting only in decision space may not provide accurate estimates of changes in DMOP. In response to this issue, a two-space based prediction strategy (TSP) is proposed, which is adapted to environmental changes. First, a denoising autoencoder search model is built, which is predicted from the perspective of decision space. Then, directly predict individuals in the objective space. After that, an improved inverse model is designed, which is to map the predicted individuals to the decision space. Finally, new solutions predicted based on decision and objective spaces are gathered together to form the initial population. The experimental results display that TSP is effective in handling most DMOP test cases.

articleTitle: Query Reformulator And Contrastive Answer Ranker For Conversational Question Answering Over Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Conversational KGQA (Knowledge Graph Question Answering) is a sequential process of question-answering over a knowledge graph (KG). Conversational KGQA involves follow-up questions that are presented in anaphoric or abbreviated form, known as ellipsis. Another challenge is the difficulty in selecting corrects answer for follow-up questions from a large number of candidate answers from KGs. This paper aims to tackle the challenge of alleviating the ellipsis phenomena and selecting correct answers from copious candidates. We present a module called CSR, which effectively merges information-retrieval-based method with pretrained language models. This module aims to identify the most relevant entity for elliptical questions based on instructional templates and subsequently rephrase the questions. Additionally, we propose a contrastive answer ranker to address the challenge of selecting the correct answer from copious candidates by leveraging the relationship between the questions and answers. Leveraging fewer trainable parameters, our method outperforms baselines on ConvQuestions and surpass the F1-Score metric of state-of-the-art on ConvRef dataset.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Analysis Method for Distribution Network Flexibility Considering Typical Scene Set
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: To select an effective regulation scheme to enhance the flexibility of distribution networks, the article proposes a distribution network flexibility analysis method considering distributed energy access scenarios. First, a two stage based K-means clustering method is used to extract typical scenario samples, second, the correlation between the distribution network economic dispatch optimization model taking flexibility resources into account and the distribution network flexibility indexes is analyzed, and finally, the computational feasible solution method based on dynamic trajectories is used to analyze the typical scenario samples for the flexibility of the distribution network, and to provide a reference for the selection of the regulation scheme for the flexibility improvement of the distribution network. The practicality of the two-stage based K-means clustering method in extracting typical scenarios and the effectiveness of the distribution network flexibility analysis method proposed in the article are numerically verified in the 33 Bus distribution network.

articleTitle: Temporal Action Localization : A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Temporal action localization(TAL) is a fundamental and extremely challenging problem in video understanding in computer vision. The growth of online media has led to the continuous generation of a vast amount of untrimmed videos, which has resulted in substantial research attention on TAL in recent years. This article presents a review of the main advances in the TAL field, covering both traditional methods and deep learning techniques. The article also reviews emerging research findings in areas such as weakly-supervised learning and multimodal data processing, analyzing and contrasting the advantages of these models. This paper presents commonly used datasets and evaluation metrics that are employed in this task. Finally, this article summarizes the current challenges in the field of TAL and suggests future directions for the development of TAL research.

articleTitle: Quality-Cost Trade-off on Constructing Logical Views for Vehicular Cyber-Physical Systems: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: With the development of sensing technologies, vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communications, edge computing paradigm, vehicular cyber-physical systems (VCPS) are emerging as the most fundamental platform for realizing future intelligent transportation systems (ITSs). In particular, the construction of logical views at the edge nodes based on heterogeneous information sensing and uploading are critical to the realization of VCPS. However, a higher-quality view in terms of timeliness and accuracy may require higher cost on sensing and uploading. In view of this, this paper is dedicated to striking a balance between the quality and the cost for constructing logical views of VCPS. Specifically, we first derive an information sensing model based on multi-class M/G/1 priority queue and a data uploading model based on reliability-guaranteed vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communications. On this basis, we design two metrics, namely, age of view (AoV) and cost of view (CoV), simultaneously. Then, we formulate a bi-objective problem to minimize the CoV and AoV. Further, we propose a distributed distributional deep deterministic policy gradient (D4PG) solution to determine sensing information, frequency, uploading priority, transmission power, and V2I bandwidth. Finally, we build a simulation model and give a comprehensive performance evaluation, and the simulation results conclusively demonstrate the superiority of the proposed solution.
